name: Secondary Vasculitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, laboratory, and histopathological correlation

criteria.description: Presence of underlying infection, malignancy, or autoimmune disease known to trigger vasculitis
Biopsy demonstrating vessel wall inflammation consistent with vasculitis
Clinical signs and symptoms consistent with vasculitis affecting one or more organ systems
Exclusion of primary vasculitis or other mimicking conditions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of underlying trigger plus histopathological confirmation of vasculitis and compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical, laboratory, and histopathological findings; no universally accepted formal criteria exist.

pathognomonic.notes: Commonly seen in cutaneous small vessel involvement

searchTerms: blood vessel wall death on biopsy

laboratory: Positive ANCA or other autoantibodies depending on underlying disease
Evidence of infection or malignancy in relevant tests
imaging: Angiography showing vessel irregularities or occlusions
MRI or CT demonstrating organ involvement
genetic: No specific genetic markers; genetic predisposition may be related to underlying autoimmune diseases
other: Histopathology showing leukocytoclastic vasculitis or necrotizing vasculitis

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of underlying infection, malignancy, or autoimmune trigger
Presence of cardiac vegetations on echocardiogram
Vasculitis-like symptoms secondary to septic emboli
Histopathology may be similar but clinical context differs

redFlags: Severe neurological deficits such as mononeuritis multiplex or stroke
references: Jennette JC, Falk RJ, Bacon PA, et al. 2012 Revised International Chapel Hill Consensus Conference Nomenclature of Vasculitides. Arthritis Rheum. 2013 Jan;65(1):1-11.
